newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips soar in heavy post-holiday rally.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips soar in heavy post-holiday rally.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur stock investors returned to the market in a buying mood, boosting the Composite Index up by one percent as they snapped up selected blue chips and second- and third-liners.

Resuming from a four-day closure for the Chinese New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr festivals, the Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed up 12.47 points to 1,254.42. It hit an intraday high of 1,260.10 earlier in the day.
Institutional buying in motor stocks and retail focus on "penny stocks" valued at under five ringgit accounted for most of the day's business, an institutional dealer said.
Volume was hefty at over 448 million, with the bulk of 416 million focused on the main board.
Interest was thin on small-capitalisation sector, where the Second Board index slipped 3.24 points to 613.68.
"It looks like they (institutions) were mainly concentrating on motor stocks, and the retail market is concentrating on penny stocks," said an institutional dealer with a local firm.
Another dealer said, "It's the second- and third-liners. A lot of retail investors have had enough of the Second Board. They're looking for new opportunities."
